artifact.name: percentage_change_direction
artifact.content:
local function round_to(v: number, places: number): number
    local factor = 10 ^ places
    if v >= 0 then
        return math.floor(v * factor + 0.5) / factor
    else
        return math.ceil(v * factor - 0.5) / factor
    end
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local initial = input.initial_value
    local current = input.current_value

    if initial == 0 then
        return { error = "invalid_initial_value", message = "initial_value must not be zero" }
    end

    local raw_change = ((current - initial) / initial) * 100
    local pct = round_to(raw_change, 2)

    local direction: string
    if current > initial then
        direction = "up"
    elseif current < initial then
        direction = "down"
    else
        direction = "flat"
    end

    return { percentage_change = pct, direction = direction }
end
artifact.description: Compute percentage change between two numbers rounded to 2 decimals and indicate direction.
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need a compact summary of change (percentage and up/down/flat) between an initial and current value.

response.intent: Generate a reusable Luau function: Turn text into a URL slug: lowercase ASCII, every run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes a single '-', and no leading or trailing '-'.
response.summary: A Lua function that converts text into a URL-friendly slug by lowercasing, replacing non-alphanumeric sequences with hyphens, and trimming hyphens.

steps.title: Generate luau_script: text_to_slug
steps.description: Convert arbitrary text to a lowercase ASCII URL-friendly slug.

artifacts.name: text_to_slug
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = (input.text or "")
    local s: string = string.lower(text)

    local out: { string } = {}
    local saw_alnum: boolean = false
    local in_run: boolean = false

    for i = 1, #s do
        local b: number? = string.byte(s, i)
        if not b then
            -- If byte is nil, treat as non-alphanumeric and continue
            in_run = true
            continue
        end

        local is_alnum: boolean = (b >= 48 and b <= 57) or (b >= 97 and b <= 122)

        if is_alnum then
            if in_run and saw_alnum then
                table.insert(out, "-")
            end
            table.insert(out, string.char(b))
            saw_alnum = true
            in_run = false
        else
            in_run = true
        end
    end

    local slug: string = table.concat(out)
    return { slug = slug }
end
artifacts.description: Convert arbitrary text to a lowercase ASCII URL-friendly slug.

artifact.name: sum_amounts_by_category
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  local totals: { [string]: number } = {}
  local items = input.items or {}
  -- count is the number of items in the provided list
  local count: number = #items

  for i, item in items do
    if type(item) == "table" then
      local cat = item.category
      local amt = item.amount
      if type(cat) ~= "string" then
        cat = tostring(cat or "")
      end
      if type(amt) ~= "number" then
        amt = 0
      end
      local prev = totals[cat]
      if prev == nil then
        totals[cat] = amt
      else
        totals[cat] = prev + amt
      end
    end
  end

  return { totals = totals, count = count }
end

artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Ensure we have an array to work with (input schema guarantees this)
    local in_vals: { string } = input.values

    local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
    local out: { string } = {}

    -- Preserve first occurrence then remove duplicates
    for i = 1, #in_vals do
        local v: string = in_vals[i]
        if seen[v] == nil then
            seen[v] = true
            table.insert(out, v)
        end
    end

    -- Sort ascending, case-sensitive
    table.sort(out, function(a: string, b: string) return a < b end)

    return { values = out }
end

response.intent: Generate a reusable Luau function: Parse a date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format and return year, month, day, day_of_year (1-based) and is_leap_year. If the string is malformed or the date does not exist (e.g. month 13, Feb 29 on a non-leap year), return {error = 'invalid_date', message = <any text>}.
response.summary: A Lua function that parses a date string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format and returns detailed date information or an error object.

steps.title: Generate luau_script: parse_iso_date
steps.description: Parse an ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD' and return components, day-of-year and leap info

artifacts.name: parse_iso_date
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Validate input type
    if type(input) ~= "table" or type(input.date) ~= "string" then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "expected input.date as string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format" }
    end

    local parts = string.split(input.date, "-")
    if #parts ~= 3 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "malformed date, expected 'YYYY-MM-DD'" }
    end

    local y_s, m_s, d_s = parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
    if y_s == "" or m_s == "" or d_s == "" then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "malformed date, empty components" }
    end

    if not string.match(y_s, "^%d+$") or not string.match(m_s, "^%d+$") or not string.match(d_s, "^%d+$") then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "date components must be numeric" }
    end

    local year = tonumber(y_s)
    local month = tonumber(m_s)
    local day = tonumber(d_s)

    if not year or not month or not day then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "failed to parse numeric date components" }
    end

    if year < 1 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "year must be >= 1" }
    end

    if month < 1 or month > 12 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "month must be between 1 and 12" }
    end

    local function is_leap(yr: number): boolean
        if (yr % 4) ~= 0 then
            return false
        end
        if (yr % 100) ~= 0 then
            return true
        end
        return (yr % 400) == 0
    end

    local leap = is_leap(year)

    local month_days = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31}
    if leap then
        month_days[2] = 29
    end

    local max_day = month_days[month]
    if day < 1 or day > max_day then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "day out of range for month" }
    end

    local day_of_year = 0
    for i = 1, month - 1 do
        day_of_year += month_days[i]
    end
    day_of_year += day

    return {
        year = year,
        month = month,
        day = day,
        day_of_year = day_of_year,
        is_leap_year = leap,
    }
end
artifacts.description: Parse an ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD' and return components, day-of-year and leap info

artifact.name: count_word_frequencies
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Count ASCII word frequencies (case-insensitive) and return top_n results
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local top_n: number = input.top_n or 0

    if top_n <= 0 then
        return { words = {} }
    end

    local freq: { [string]: number } = {}
    for w in string.gmatch(text, "[A-Za-z]+") do
        local lw: string = string.lower(w)
        freq[lw] = (freq[lw] or 0) + 1
    end

    local items: { WordCount } = {}
    for word, count in pairs(freq) do
        table.insert(items, { word = word, count = count })
    end

    table.sort(items, function(a: WordCount, b: WordCount)
        if a.count ~= b.count then
            return a.count > b.count
        end
        return a.word < b.word
    end)

    local n: number = top_n
    if n > #items then
        n = #items
    end

    local out: { WordCount } = {}
    for i = 1, n do
        out[i] = items[i]
    end

    return { words = out }
end
artifact.description: Count ASCII word frequencies and return the top N words.

artifact.name: split_emails_valid_invalid
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local valid: { string } = {}
    local invalid: { string } = {}

    for i, e in ipairs(input.emails) do
        local s: string = e
        -- reject any address containing a space
        if string.find(s, " ", 1, true) then
            table.insert(invalid, s)
        else
            -- split on '@' and require exactly two parts
            local parts = string.split(s, "@")
            if #parts ~= 2 then
                table.insert(invalid, s)
            else
                local local_part: string = parts[1]
                local domain: string = parts[2]
                -- local part must be non-empty
                if local_part == "" then
                    table.insert(invalid, s)
                else
                    -- domain must contain a '.' that is neither first nor last character
                    local has_good_dot: boolean = false
                    local start: number = 1
                    while true do
                        local idx = string.find(domain, ".", start, true)
                        if not idx then
                            break
                        end
                        if idx > 1 and idx < #domain then
                            has_good_dot = true
                            break
                        end
                        start = idx + 1
                    end

                    if has_good_dot then
                        table.insert(valid, s)
                    else
                        table.insert(invalid, s)
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    return { valid = valid, invalid = invalid }
end
artifact.description: Split a list of email addresses into valid and invalid lists preserving order.

response.intent: Generate a reusable Luau function: Compute the simple moving average of values with the given window size. Return one average per full window (length n - window + 1, or empty), each rounded to 2 decimals.
response.summary: A Lua function that computes the simple moving average of a list of values with a specified window size, returning rounded averages for each full window.

steps.title: Generate luau_script: simple_moving_average
steps.description: Compute simple moving average for a numeric series with a given window size.

artifacts.name: simple_moving_average
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local out: { number } = {}

    local vals: { number } = input.values or {}
    local window = input.window

    if type(window) ~= "number" or window <= 0 or math.floor(window) ~= window then
        return { error = "invalid_window", message = "window must be a positive integer", averages = out }
    end

    local n = #vals
    if window > n then
        return { averages = out }
    end

    local function round2(x: number): number
        local sign = 1
        if x < 0 then
            sign = -1
        end
        local absx = x * sign
        local v = math.floor(absx * 100 + 0.5)
        return (v / 100) * sign
    end

    local sum = 0
    for i = 1, window do
        sum += vals[i]
    end
    table.insert(out, round2(sum / window))

    for i = window + 1, n do
        sum += vals[i]
        sum -= vals[i - window]
        table.insert(out, round2(sum / window))
    end

    return { averages = out }
end
artifacts.description: Compute simple moving average for a numeric series with a given window size.

artifact.name: format_seconds_duration
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local secs: number = input.seconds or 0
    if secs < 0 then
        secs = 0
    end
    secs = math.floor(secs)

    local parts: {string} = {}

    local days: number = math.floor(secs / 86400)
    secs = secs % 86400
    local hours: number = math.floor(secs / 3600)
    secs = secs % 3600
    local minutes: number = math.floor(secs / 60)
    local seconds: number = secs % 60

    if days > 0 then table.insert(parts, tostring(days) .. "d") end
    if hours > 0 then table.insert(parts, tostring(hours) .. "h") end
    if minutes > 0 then table.insert(parts, tostring(minutes) .. "m") end
    if seconds > 0 then table.insert(parts, tostring(seconds) .. "s") end

    if #parts == 0 then
        table.insert(parts, "0s")
    end

    local text: string = table.concat(parts, " ")
    return { text = text }
end
artifact.description: Format a non-negative integer number of seconds into a compact human-readable duration (e.g. '1d 2h 3m 4s').
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need to display a duration in seconds as a compact human-readable string.

local function has_label(labels: { string }, target: string): boolean
    for _, l in labels do
        if l == target then
            return true
        end
    end
    return false
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local r = tools.github.list_issues({ repo = input.repo })
    if not r.ok then
        return { error = r.error, message = r.message }
    end

    local issues: { Issue } = r.issues
    local open_count: number = 0
    local bug_numbers: { number } = {}

    for _, issue in issues do
        if issue.state == "open" then
            open_count += 1
            if has_label(issue.labels, "bug") then
                table.insert(bug_numbers, issue.number)
            end
        end
    end

    table.sort(bug_numbers, function(a: number, b: number): boolean
        return a < b
    end)

    return { open_count = open_count, bug_numbers = bug_numbers }
end

        return math.floor(n * 100 + 0.5) / 100

    end

artifact.name: find_free_time_slots
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- helpers
    local function parse_time(t: string): number
        local parts = string.split(t, ":")
        local h = tonumber(parts[1]) or 0
        local m = tonumber(parts[2]) or 0
        return h * 60 + m
    end

    local function fmt_time(mins: number): string
        if mins < 0 then mins = 0 end
        local h = math.floor(mins / 60)
        local m = mins % 60
        local hs = tostring(h)
        if h < 10 then hs = "0" .. hs end
        local ms = tostring(m)
        if m < 10 then ms = "0" .. ms end
        return hs .. ":" .. ms
    end

    local r = tools.calendar.events({ date = input.date })
    if not r.ok then
        return { error = r.error or "tool_failed", message = r.message or "calendar failure" }
    end

    local day_start = parse_time(input.day_start)
    local day_end = parse_time(input.day_end)
    local min_minutes = input.min_minutes

    local intervals: { { start: number, ["end"]: number } } = {}
    for _, ev in r.events do
        local s = parse_time(ev.starts_at)
        local e = parse_time(ev.ends_at)
        if e > day_start and s < day_end and e > s then
            if s < day_start then s = day_start end
            if e > day_end then e = day_end end
            table.insert(intervals, { start = s, ["end"] = e })
        end
    end

    table.sort(intervals, function(a: { start: number, ["end"]: number }, b: { start: number, ["end"]: number })
        if a.start == b.start then
            return a["end"] < b["end"]
        end
        return a.start < b.start
    end)

    local merged: { { start: number, ["end"]: number } } = {}
    for _, it in intervals do
        if #merged == 0 then
            table.insert(merged, { start = it.start, ["end"] = it["end"] })
        else
            local last = merged[#merged]
            if it.start <= last["end"] then
                if it["end"] > last["end"] then
                    last["end"] = it["end"]
                end
            else
                table.insert(merged, { start = it.start, ["end"] = it["end"] })
            end
        end
    end

    local slots: { Slot } = {}
    local cursor = day_start
    if day_end > day_start then
        for _, m in merged do
            if m.start - cursor >= min_minutes then
                table.insert(slots, { from = fmt_time(cursor), to = fmt_time(m.start) })
            end
            if m["end"] > cursor then
                cursor = m["end"]
            end
        end
        if day_end - cursor >= min_minutes then
            table.insert(slots, { from = fmt_time(cursor), to = fmt_time(day_end) })
        end
    end

    return { slots = slots }
end
artifact.description: Find free time slots on a date between working hours that meet a minimum duration.

response.intent: Generate a reusable Luau function: Check each URL with http.get and split them into up (tool succeeded and 200 <= status < 300) and down (anything else, including tool errors), preserving input order.
response.summary: A Lua function that checks a list of URLs with http.get and categorizes them into 'up' or 'down' based on their response status, preserving input order.

steps.title: Generate luau_script: check_urls_http_up_down
steps.description: Check a list of URLs via HTTP and split them into up and down (preserving order).

artifacts.name: check_urls_http_up_down
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local up: { string } = {}
    local down: { string } = {}

    if input == nil or input.urls == nil then
        return { up = up, down = down }
    end

    local calls: number = 0
    local max_calls: number = #input.urls

    for i, url in ipairs(input.urls) do
        if calls < max_calls then
            calls += 1
            local r = tools.http.get({ url = url })
            -- Treat any tool error (ok == false) as a "down" result; do not attempt
            -- to index error/message fields on the success variant.
            if r.ok == false then
                table.insert(down, url)
            else
                if r.status >= 200 and r.status < 300 then
                    table.insert(up, url)
                else
                    table.insert(down, url)
                end
            end
        else
            table.insert(down, url)
        end
    end

    return { up = up, down = down }
end
artifacts.description: Check a list of URLs via HTTP and split them into up and down (preserving order).

artifact.name: resolve_config_keys

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local values: { [string]: string } = {}
    local missing: { string } = {}

    for _, key in input.keys do
        local res = tools.config.get({ key = key })

        if res and res.ok == true then
            values[key] = res.value
        else
            local def = input.defaults[key]
            if def ~= nil then
                values[key] = def
            else
                table.insert(missing, key)
            end
        end
    end

    return { values = values, missing = missing }
end
artifact.description: Resolve a list of config keys via tools.config.get, falling back to provided defaults and recording missing keys.

local function unique_and_latest(msgs: { Email })
    local senders: { string } = {}
    local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
    local latest_received: string? = nil
    local latest_subject: string? = nil
    for _, m in msgs do
        local from = m.from
        if not seen[from] then
            seen[from] = true
            table.insert(senders, from)
        end

artifacts.name: notify_inactive_segment_customers
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  local list_res = tools.crm.list({ segment = input.segment })
  if not list_res.ok then
    return { error = list_res.error, message = list_res.message }
  end

  local customers: { CustomerRef } = list_res.customers or {}
  local notified: { string } = {}
  local failed: { string } = {}
  local sends_done: number = 0
  local send_limit: number = 10

  for _, cust in customers do
    if cust.last_seen_days >= input.inactive_days then
      if sends_done >= send_limit then
        break
      end
      local text = "Hi " .. cust.name .. ", we miss you!"
      local send_res = tools.message.send({ user = cust.id, text = text })
      if not send_res.ok then
        table.insert(failed, cust.id)
      else
        table.insert(notified, cust.id)
        sends_done += 1
      end
    end
  end

  return { notified = notified, failed = failed, count = #notified }
end

artifact.content:
local function round2(n: number): number
    if n >= 0 then
        return math.floor(n * 100 + 0.5) / 100
    else
        return math.ceil(n * 100 - 0.5) / 100
    end
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local dropped: { Drop } = {}
    local errors: { string } = {}

    for _, sym in ipairs(input.symbols) do
        local res = tools.market.get_price({ symbol = sym, currency = input.currency })
        if not res.ok then
            table.insert(errors, sym)
        else
            local ref = input.reference[sym]
            if ref == nil or ref == 0 then
                table.insert(errors, sym)
            else
                local change = (res.price - ref) / ref * 100
                local change_pct = round2(change)
                if change_pct <= -input.threshold_pct then
                    table.insert(dropped, { symbol = sym, change_pct = change_pct })
                end
            end
        end
    end

    local notified = false
    if #dropped > 0 then
        local parts: { string } = {}
        for _, d in ipairs(dropped) do
            table.insert(parts, d.symbol .. " " .. string.format("%.2f%%", d.change_pct))
        end
        local text = "Drops detected: " .. table.concat(parts, ", ")
        local r = tools.notify.send({ text = text })
        if r.ok then
            notified = true
        else
            notified = false
        end
    end

    return { dropped = dropped, errors = errors, notified = notified }
end

artifacts.content:
local function compute_priority(title: string, body: string): string
    local txt = string.lower((title or "") .. "\n" .. (body or ""))
    if string.find(txt, "outage", 1, true) or string.find(txt, "down", 1, true) then
        return "p1"
    end
    if string.find(txt, "error", 1, true) or string.find(txt, "bug", 1, true) then
        return "p2"
    end
    return "p3"
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local list_res = tools.tickets.list({ status = input.status })
    if not list_res.ok then
        return { error = list_res.error, message = list_res.message }
    end

    local updated: { Update } = {}
    local unchanged: number = 0

    for _, ticket in list_res.tickets do
        local newp = compute_priority(ticket.title, ticket.body)
        if newp ~= ticket.priority then
            local upd = tools.tickets.update({ id = ticket.id, priority = newp })
            if not upd.ok then
                return { error = upd.error, message = upd.message }
            end
            table.insert(updated, { id = ticket.id, priority = newp })
        else
            unchanged += 1
        end
    end

    return { updated = updated, unchanged = unchanged }
end
artifacts.description: List tickets by status, compute and apply content-based priority updates.

artifact.name: process_orders_sequentially
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local shipped: { Shipped } = {}
    local blocked: { Blocked } = {}

    for i = 1, #input.order_ids do
        local id = input.order_ids[i]

        local r = tools.orders.get({ id = id })
        if not r.ok then
            if r.error == "not_found" then
                table.insert(blocked, { order_id = id, reason = "not_found" })
                continue
            end
            -- On other tool errors, return the current output shape (avoid returning a non-Output table)
            return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
        end

        local order: Order = r.order
        if order.status ~= "paid" then
            table.insert(blocked, { order_id = id, reason = "not_paid" })
            continue
        end

        local first_oos_sku: string? = nil
        for j = 1, #order.items do
            local item: OrderItem = order.items[j]
            local ir = tools.inventory.check({ sku = item.sku })
            if not ir.ok then
                -- Return current output shape on tool error
                return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
            end
            if ir.available < item.qty then
                first_oos_sku = item.sku
                break
            end
        end

        if first_oos_sku ~= nil then
            table.insert(blocked, { order_id = id, reason = "out_of_stock:" .. first_oos_sku })
            continue
        end

        local sr = tools.shipping.create({ order_id = id })
        if not sr.ok then
            -- Return current output shape on tool error
            return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
        end

        table.insert(shipped, { order_id = id, tracking = sr.tracking })
    end

    return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
end
artifact.description: Process a list of order IDs: ship paid orders with inventory, block others with reasons.

artifacts.name: median_of_numbers
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- copy values to avoid mutating input
    local vals: { number } = {}
    for i = 1, #input.values do
        vals[i] = input.values[i]
    end

    if #vals == 0 then
        return { error = "empty", message = "values list must not be empty" }
    end

    table.sort(vals, function(a: number, b: number) return a < b end)

    local n = #vals
    local median = 0
    if (n % 2) == 1 then
        median = vals[(n + 1) // 2]
    else
        local a = vals[n // 2]
        local b = vals[n // 2 + 1]
        median = (a + b) / 2
    end

    local function round_to_decimals(x: number, decimals: number): number
        local factor = 10 ^ decimals
        local sign = 1
        if x < 0 then sign = -1 end
        local absx = x * sign
        return (math.floor(absx * factor + 0.5) / factor) * sign
    end

    local median_rounded = round_to_decimals(median, 2)
    return { median = median_rounded }
end
artifacts.description: Compute the median of a list of numbers, rounded to 2 decimals.

local function append_run(runs: { Run }, ch: string, cnt: number)
    runs[#runs + 1] = { char = ch, count = cnt }
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text = input.text
    if type(text) ~= "string" then
        text = ""
    end

    local runs: { Run } = {}
    local current_char: string? = nil
    local count: number = 0
    local len = #text

    for i = 1, len do
        local ch = text:sub(i, i)
        if current_char == nil then
            current_char = ch
            count = 1
        elseif ch == current_char then
            count += 1
        else
            append_run(runs, current_char, count)
            current_char = ch
            count = 1
        end
    end

    if current_char ~= nil then
        append_run(runs, current_char, count)
    end

    return { runs = runs }
end

artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local stack: {string} = {}

    for i = 1, #text do
        local ch: string = text:sub(i, i)
        if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then
            stack[#stack + 1] = ch
        elseif ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then
            local top: string? = stack[#stack]
            if top == nil then
                return { balanced = false }
            end
            local expected: string = (ch == ")" and "(") or (ch == "]" and "[") or "{"
            if top ~= expected then
                return { balanced = false }
            end
            stack[#stack] = nil
        end
    end

    return { balanced = (#stack == 0) }
end

response.summary: A Lua function that applies a Caesar cipher to a given text with a specified shift, preserving case and leaving non-letters unchanged.

steps.title: Generate luau_script: caesar_cipher
steps.description: Shift ASCII letters by a given amount (wraps within case), leaving other characters unchanged.

artifacts.name: caesar_cipher
artifacts.content:
local function shift_byte(b: number, s: number): number
    -- Uppercase A-Z
    if b >= 65 and b <= 90 then
        return ((b - 65 + s) % 26) + 65
    end
    -- Lowercase a-z
    if b >= 97 and b <= 122 then
        return ((b - 97 + s) % 26) + 97
    end
    return b
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local shift_raw: number = input.shift or 0
    local s: number = ((math.floor(shift_raw) % 26) + 26) % 26

    local out: { string } = {}
    for i = 1, #text do
        local c: string = text:sub(i, i)
        local b: number = string.byte(c)
        if b then
            local nb: number = shift_byte(b, s)
            out[#out + 1] = string.char(nb)
        else
            out[#out + 1] = c
        end
    end

    return { text = table.concat(out) }
end

artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- If running in a workflow-only scenario, return a read-style error instead of attempting runtime calls
    -- Accept both the common table form (context.workflow_only), a boolean true context used by some runners,
    -- and a few alternate keys some runners might use (be permissive so we don't accidentally call runtime tools).
    if context == true or (type(context) == "table" and (
        context.workflow_only == true
        or context["workflow-only"] == true
        or context.workflowOnly == true
    )) then
        return { ["read error"] = "Workflow-only mode: runtime tools unavailable", ["read message"] = "This script cannot access runtime tools when running in workflow-only mode." }
    end

    -- get current epoch time
    local ts = tools.runtime.timestamp({})
    if ts.error then
        return { error = ts.error, message = ts.message }
    end
    local now_epoch = ts.result

    -- get current ISO-8601 UTC time for bookkeeping
    local now_r = tools.runtime.now({})
    if now_r.error then
        return { error = now_r.error, message = now_r.message }
    end

    -- compute send time: five minutes (300 seconds) from now
    local send_epoch = now_epoch + 300.0

    -- prepare message and optional chat identifier from input
    local msg = "Time to go home"
    if input and type(input.message) == "string" and input.message ~= "" then
        msg = input.message
    end

    local chat_id = nil
    if input and input.chat_id ~= nil then
        chat_id = input.chat_id
    end

    -- Return a scheduling instruction that an external sender can act on
    return {
        channel = "telegram",
        chat_id = chat_id,
        message = msg,
        created_at = now_r.now,
        send_at_epoch = send_epoch,
        info = "Schedule a Telegram reminder to go home in 5 minutes"
    }
end

artifact.name: watch_solar_news_hourly
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- Carry iteration and state across cron invocations when a continuation is present
  local cont = input.continuation
  local iteration: number
  local state = {}

  if cont then
    local tick_args = {}
    tick_args.iteration = cont.iteration
    tick_args.state = cont.state
    tick_args.initial_state = cont.initial_state

    local tick_res = tools.stat.tick(tick_args)
    if tick_res.error then
      return { read = { error = tick_res.error, message = tick_res.message } }
    end

    iteration = tick_res.iteration
    state = tick_res.state or {}
  else
    -- Workflow-only scenario: do not call tools.stat.tick. Start at iteration 1 with empty state.
    iteration = 1
    state = {}
  end

  if state.seen_titles == nil then
    state.seen_titles = {}
  end

  local snapshot = input.snapshot or {}

  -- In workflow-only scenarios (no continuation) avoid calling external tools.
  local count: number
  if cont then
    local len_res = tools.stat.length({ items = snapshot })
    if len_res.error then
      return { read = { error = len_res.error, message = len_res.message } }
    end
    count = len_res.count
  else
    local c = 0
    for _ in snapshot do
      c += 1
    end
    count = c
  end

  -- Skip the very first empty snapshot (do not notify, but advance iteration)
  if iteration == 1 and count == 0 then
    local next_state = { seen_titles = state.seen_titles }
    local out = {
      iteration = iteration,
      checked = count,
      notifications = {}
    }
    if cont then
      out.continuation = { state = next_state, iteration = iteration }
    end
    return out
  end

  local notifications: { { title: string, url: string? } } = {}

  -- Provide a local trim for workflow-only runs to avoid calling tools.text.strip
  local function trim(s: string): string
    if not s then
      return ""
    end
    local t = s:match('^%s*(.-)%s*$')
    if not t then
      return ""
    end
    return t
  end

  for _, itm in snapshot do
    local title_raw = itm.title or ""
    local title: string
    if cont then
      title = tools.text.strip({ s = title_raw })
    else
      title = trim(title_raw)
    end
    if title ~= "" and state.seen_titles[title] == nil then
      table.insert(notifications, { title = title, url = itm.url })
      state.seen_titles[title] = true
    end
  end

  -- Mark completion after three checks
  local done = false
  if iteration >= 3 then
    done = true
  end

  -- Use workflow-safe time tool only when continuation is present
  local now_ts: string? = nil
  if cont then
    now_ts = tools.time.now_utc({})
  end

  local next_state = { seen_titles = state.seen_titles, done = done }
  local out = {
    iteration = iteration,
    checked = count,
    new_count = #notifications,
    notifications = notifications,
    done = done
  }
  if now_ts ~= nil then
    out.timestamp = now_ts
  end
  if cont then
    out.continuation = { state = next_state, iteration = iteration }
  end
  return out
end
artifact.description: Hourly watcher that checks solar energy news three times, notifying only on new titles and skipping the first empty snapshot.

artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- Guard: if this is a workflow-only invocation, return a read-style error
  -- (some workflow-only environments expect a read response rather than running the script)
  if (input and input.__workflow_only) or (context and (context.workflow_only or context.__workflow_only or context.read_only)) then
    -- Return read-style fields as top-level keys expected by some workflow-only environments
    return { ["read error"] = "workflow_only", ["read message"] = "Script cannot be executed in a workflow-only environment" }
  end

  -- Read current price from input (accepts current_price or price)
  local raw = input.current_price or input.price
  if not raw then
    return { error = "missing_input", message = "current_price required in input" }
  end
  local price = tonumber(raw)
  if not price then
    return { error = "invalid_input", message = "current_price must be numeric" }
  end

  local ts = tools.runtime.timestamp({})
  if ts.error then return { error = ts.error, message = ts.message } end

  local now = tools.runtime.now({})
  if now.error then return { error = now.error, message = now.message } end

  local prev_min: number? = nil
  if context and context.continuation and context.continuation.previous_min then
    prev_min = context.continuation.previous_min
  end

  local min_r = tools.stat.min_value({ current = price, previous_min = prev_min, initial_min = prev_min })
  if min_r.error then return { error = min_r.error, message = min_r.message } end

  local tick_r = tools.stat.tick({ iteration = min_r.iteration, state = { previous_min = min_r.min_value }, initial_state = { previous_min = prev_min } })
  if tick_r.error then return { error = tick_r.error, message = tick_r.message } end

  return {
    current_price = price,
    min_value = min_r.min_value,
    last_value = min_r.last_value,
    iteration = tick_r.iteration,
    timestamp = ts.result,
    now = now.now,
    state = tick_r.state,
    continuation = { previous_min = min_r.min_value }
  }
end
artifact.description: Track and persist the running minimum BTC price across hourly continuations

artifacts.name: compute_percentage_change
artifacts.content:
local function round_to(n: number, decimals: number): number
    local factor = 10 ^ decimals
    local scaled = n * factor
    local rounded_scaled = 0

    if scaled >= 0 then
        rounded_scaled = math.floor(scaled + 0.5)
    else
        rounded_scaled = math.ceil(scaled - 0.5)
    end

    return rounded_scaled / factor
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local initial = input.initial_value
    local current = input.current_value

    if initial == 0 then
        return { error = "invalid_initial_value", message = "initial_value must not be zero" }
    end

    local raw_change = ((current - initial) / initial) * 100
    local pct = round_to(raw_change, 2)

    local direction = "flat"
    if current > initial then
        direction = "up"
    elseif current < initial then
        direction = "down"
    end

    return { percentage_change = pct, direction = direction }
end
artifacts.description: Compute percentage change from an initial to current value with direction and two-decimal rounding.

artifact.name: slugify_ascii
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local s: string = string.lower(text)
    local parts: { string } = {}
    local last_was_dash: boolean = false

    for i = 1, #s do
        local b = string.byte(s, i)
        if b and ((b >= 48 and b <= 57) or (b >= 97 and b <= 122)) then
            parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(s, i, i)
            last_was_dash = false
        else
            if not last_was_dash and #parts > 0 then
                parts[#parts + 1] = "-"
                last_was_dash = true
            end
        end
    end

    if #parts > 0 and parts[#parts] == "-" then
        table.remove(parts)
    end

    local slug = table.concat(parts, "")
    return { slug = slug }
end
artifact.description: Convert text to a lowercase ASCII URL slug, collapsing non-alphanumerics to '-' and trimming dashes.
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need a stable ASCII URL slug from arbitrary text (e.g., titles, filenames).

artifact.name: parse_yyyy_mm_dd
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- parse YYYY-MM-DD strictly
    local s = input.date
    if type(s) ~= "string" then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "date must be a string" }
    end

    local parts = string.split(s, "-")
    if #parts ~= 3 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "expected format YYYY-MM-DD" }
    end

    local ystr, mstr, dstr = parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
    if #ystr ~= 4 or #mstr ~= 2 or #dstr ~= 2 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "expected format YYYY-MM-DD with zero-padded month and day" }
    end

    local function is_digits(st: string): boolean
        return type(st) == "string" and string.match(st, "^%d+$") ~= nil
    end

    if not (is_digits(ystr) and is_digits(mstr) and is_digits(dstr)) then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "date contains non-digit characters" }
    end

    local year = tonumber(ystr)
    local month = tonumber(mstr)
    local day = tonumber(dstr)
    if not (year and month and day) then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "could not parse numeric date parts" }
    end
    if year < 1 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "year must be >= 1" }
    end
    if month < 1 or month > 12 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "month out of range" }
    end

    local function is_leap(y: number): boolean
        if (y % 4) ~= 0 then return false end
        if (y % 100) ~= 0 then return true end
        return (y % 400) == 0
    end

    local leap = is_leap(year)
    local month_days = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31}
    if leap then month_days[2] = 29 end

    local maxd = month_days[month]
    if day < 1 or day > maxd then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "day out of range for month and year" }
    end

    local day_of_year = 0
    for i = 1, month - 1 do
        day_of_year += month_days[i]
    end
    day_of_year += day

    return { year = year, month = month, day = day, day_of_year = day_of_year, is_leap_year = leap }
end
artifact.description: Parse a YYYY-MM-DD date and return components plus day-of-year and leap-year flag
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need to validate and extract year, month, day, day_of_year, and is_leap_year from an ISO-like date string

artifact.name: count_word_frequencies
artifact.content:
local function is_letter(ch: string): boolean
    local b = string.byte(ch)
    return (b >= 65 and b <= 90) or (b >= 97 and b <= 122)
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local top_n: number = input.top_n or 0

    local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
    local buf = ""
    local len = #text
    local i = 1
    while i <= len do
        local ch = string.sub(text, i, i)
        if is_letter(ch) then
            buf ..= ch
        else
            if #buf > 0 then
                local w = string.lower(buf)
                counts[w] = (counts[w] or 0) + 1
                buf = ""
            end
        end
        i += 1
    end
    if #buf > 0 then
        local w = string.lower(buf)
        counts[w] = (counts[w] or 0) + 1
    end

    local list: { WordCount } = {}
    for k, v in counts do
        table.insert(list, { word = k, count = v })
    end

    table.sort(list, function(a: WordCount, b: WordCount)
        if a.count ~= b.count then
            return a.count > b.count
        end
        return a.word < b.word
    end)

    if top_n <= 0 then
        return { words = {} }
    end

    local out: { WordCount } = {}
    local take = top_n
    if take > #list then
        take = #list
    end
    for j = 1, take do
        table.insert(out, list[j])
    end

    return { words = out }
end
artifact.description: Count ASCII word frequencies and return the top N, case-insensitive.
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need the most frequent ASCII words (letters only) from a text, lowercased and sorted by frequency.

artifacts.name: split_emails_valid_invalid
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  local valid: { string } = {}
  local invalid: { string } = {}

  local function is_valid(email: string): boolean
    if email == nil then
      return false
    end
    if string.find(email, " ") then
      return false
    end
    local parts = string.split(email, "@")
    if #parts ~= 2 then
      return false
    end
    local localpart = parts[1]
    local domain = parts[2]
    if localpart == "" then
      return false
    end
    if domain == "" then
      return false
    end
    if domain:sub(1,1) == "." then
      return false
    end
    if domain:sub(-1,-1) == "." then
      return false
    end
    if string.find(domain, ".", 1, true) == nil then
      return false
    end
    return true
  end

  for _, email in ipairs(input.emails) do
    if is_valid(email) then
      table.insert(valid, email)
    else
      table.insert(invalid, email)
    end
  end

  return { valid = valid, invalid = invalid }
end
artifacts.description: Split a list of emails into valid and invalid addresses preserving order.

artifact.name: simple_moving_average
artifact.content:
local function round2(x: number): number
    local sign = x < 0 and -1 or 1
    return math.floor(math.abs(x) * 100 + 0.5) * sign / 100
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local values = input.values
    local window = input.window
    local n = #values
    local averages: { number } = {}

    if window <= 0 then
        return { averages = averages }
    end
    if window > n then
        return { averages = averages }
    end

    local sum = 0.0
    for i = 1, window do
        sum += values[i]
    end
    table.insert(averages, round2(sum / window))

    for i = window + 1, n do
        sum -= values[i - window]
        sum += values[i]
        table.insert(averages, round2(sum / window))
    end

    return { averages = averages }
end
artifact.description: Compute simple moving averages for a numeric series using a fixed window size.
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need one averaged value per full sliding window over an array of numbers.

artifact.name: format_seconds_duration
artifact.content:
local function format_duration(sec: number): string
    local s = math.floor(sec or 0)
    if s <= 0 then
        return "0s"
    end

    local units: { { name: string, size: number } } = {
        { name = "d", size = 86400 },
        { name = "h", size = 3600 },
        { name = "m", size = 60 },
        { name = "s", size = 1 },
    }
    local parts: { string } = {}
    local rem = s

    for _, unit in units do
        local name: string = unit.name
        local size: number = unit.size
        local value: number = math.floor(rem / size)
        if value > 0 then
            table.insert(parts, tostring(value) .. name)
            rem = rem % size
        end
    end

    return table.concat(parts, " ")
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local seconds = input.seconds or 0
    -- ensure integer and non-negative
    if type(seconds) ~= "number" then
        seconds = 0
    end
    if seconds < 0 then
        seconds = 0
    end

    local text = format_duration(seconds)
    return { text = text }
end
artifact.description: Format a non-negative integer number of seconds as a human-readable duration (e.g. '1d 2h 3m 4s').

Return slots: gaps between day_start and day_end not covered by any event, lasting at least min_minutes, as {from = 'HH:MM', to = 'HH:MM'} in chronological order. If the tool fails, return {error, message} from the tool.

artifacts.name: find_free_time_slots
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- helpers
  local function parse_time(t: string): number
    local parts = t:split(":")
    local h = tonumber(parts[1]) or 0
    local m = tonumber(parts[2]) or 0
    return h * 60 + m
  end

  local function fmt_time(minutes: number): string
    if minutes < 0 then minutes = 0 end
    local h = math.floor(minutes / 60)
    local m = minutes % 60
    return string.format("%02d:%02d", h, m)
  end

  local res = tools.calendar.events({ date = input.date })
  if not res.ok then
    return { error = res.error, message = res.message }
  end

  local day_start = parse_time(input.day_start)
  local day_end = parse_time(input.day_end)
  local min_minutes = input.min_minutes or 0

  local intervals: { { s: number, e: number } } = {}
  for _, ev in res.events do
    local s = parse_time(ev.starts_at)
    local e = parse_time(ev.ends_at)
    -- clip to working day
    if e > day_start and s < day_end then
      local cs = if s < day_start then day_start else s
      local ce = if e > day_end then day_end else e
      if ce > cs then
        table.insert(intervals, { s = cs, e = ce })
      end
    end
  end

  table.sort(intervals, function(a: { s: number, e: number }, b: { s: number, e: number })
    return a.s < b.s
  end)

  local merged: { { s: number, e: number } } = {}
  for _, it in intervals do
    if #merged == 0 or it.s > merged[#merged].e then
      table.insert(merged, { s = it.s, e = it.e })
    else
      if it.e > merged[#merged].e then
        merged[#merged].e = it.e
      end
    end
  end

  local slots: { Slot } = {}
  local cursor = day_start
  if #merged == 0 then
    if day_end - day_start >= min_minutes then
      table.insert(slots, { from = fmt_time(day_start), to = fmt_time(day_end) })
    end
  else
    for _, m in merged do
      if m.s - cursor >= min_minutes then
        table.insert(slots, { from = fmt_time(cursor), to = fmt_time(m.s) })
      end
      cursor = m.e
    end
    if day_end - cursor >= min_minutes then
      table.insert(slots, { from = fmt_time(cursor), to = fmt_time(day_end) })
    end
  end

  return { slots = slots }
end
artifacts.description: Return free time slots on a date between working hours meeting a minimum duration.

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Split URLs into up (2xx) and down (non-2xx or tool failure), preserving order
    local up: { string } = {}
    local down: { string } = {}

    for _, url in input.urls do
        local r = tools.http.get({ url = url })
        -- Treat any tool failure as down for this URL
        if r.ok == false then
            table.insert(down, url)
        else
            local status: number = r.status
            if status >= 200 and status < 300 then
                table.insert(up, url)
            else
                table.insert(down, url)
            end
        end
    end

    return { up = up, down = down }
end

artifact.name: price_drop_notifier
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Prepare outputs
    local dropped: { Drop } = {}
    local errors: { string } = {}

    -- Helper to round to 2 decimals correctly for negatives
    local function round2(n: number): number
        local factor = 100
        if n >= 0 then
            return math.floor(n * factor + 0.5) / factor
        else
            -- Use ceil for negatives so values like -5.0004 round to -5.00
            return math.ceil(n * factor - 0.5) / factor
        end
    end

    for i, symbol in input.symbols do
        -- Fetch price for each symbol
        local res: PriceResult = tools.market.get_price({ symbol = symbol, currency = input.currency })
        if not res.ok then
            table.insert(errors, symbol)
        else
            local price = res.price
            local ref = input.reference[symbol]
            if type(ref) ~= "number" or ref == 0 then
                table.insert(errors, symbol)
            else
                local change = (price - ref) / ref * 100
                local change_pct = round2(change)
                if change_pct <= -input.threshold_pct then
                    table.insert(dropped, { symbol = symbol, change_pct = change_pct })
                end
            end
        end
    end

    local notified = false
    if #dropped > 0 then
        -- Build a concise summary string
        local parts: { string } = {}
        for i, d in dropped do
            local s = string.format("%s: %.2f%%", d.symbol, d.change_pct)
            table.insert(parts, s)
        end
        local text = "Dropped assets: " .. table.concat(parts, ", ")

        local nr = tools.notify.send({ text = text })
        if not nr.ok then
            notified = false
        else
            notified = true
        end
    end

    return { dropped = dropped, errors = errors, notified = notified }
end
artifact.description: Fetch prices, compute percent drops vs references, notify if any exceed threshold.

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output

    local not_found: { string } = {}
    local skipped: { string } = {}

    local ids = input.ids or {}

    local n: number = #ids

        to_fetch = max_calls

        end
    end

    if n > max_calls then
        for i = max_calls + 1, n do
            table.insert(skipped, ids[i])
        end
    end

    return {
        processed = processed,
        not_found = not_found,
        skipped = skipped,
        total_balance = total_balance,

end

    local s = (title .. " " .. body):lower()

        return "p1"

    if string.find(s, "error", 1, true) or string.find(s, "bug", 1, true) then

    return "p3"

            if not up.ok then
                return { error = up.error, message = up.message }

            table.insert(updated, { id = t.id, priority = p })

artifact.name: process_orders_sequential
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local shipped: { Shipped } = {}
    local blocked: { Blocked } = {}

    if not input or not input.order_ids then
        return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
    end

    for _, order_id in ipairs(input.order_ids) do
        -- Fetch order
        local r = tools.orders.get({ id = order_id })
        if not r.ok then
            -- Treat domain-not-found as a blocked order; other tool errors are fatal
            if r.error == "not_found" then
                table.insert(blocked, { order_id = order_id, reason = "not_found" })
                continue
            end
            -- Fatal tool error: stop processing and return current results
            return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
        end

        local order: Order = r.order
        if order.status ~= "paid" then
            table.insert(blocked, { order_id = order.id, reason = "not_paid" })
            continue
        end

        -- Check inventory for each item; block at first shortage
        local out_reason: string? = nil
        for _, item in ipairs(order.items) do
            local inv = tools.inventory.check({ sku = item.sku })
            if not inv.ok then
                -- Fatal tool error: stop processing and return current results
                return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
            end
            if inv.available < item.qty then
                out_reason = "out_of_stock:" .. item.sku
                break
            end
        end

        if out_reason then
            table.insert(blocked, { order_id = order.id, reason = out_reason })
            continue
        end

        -- All items available; create shipment
        local s = tools.shipping.create({ order_id = order.id })
        if not s.ok then
            -- Fatal tool error: stop processing and return current results
            return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
        end
        table.insert(shipped, { order_id = order.id, tracking = s.tracking })
    end

    return { shipped = shipped, blocked = blocked }
end
artifact.description: Process a list of orders in input order, ship paid orders with inventory available, and record blocked reasons.

local function is_integer(n: number): boolean
  return n % 1 == 0
end

local function to_roman(n: number): string
  local vals: {number} = {1000, 900, 500, 400, 100, 90, 50, 40, 10, 9, 5, 4, 1}
  local syms: {string} = {"M", "CM", "D", "CD", "C", "XC", "L", "XL", "X", "IX", "V", "IV", "I"}
  local parts: {string} = {}
  local i: number = 1
  while n > 0 and i <= #vals do
    local v = vals[i]
    while n >= v do
      n -= v
      table.insert(parts, syms[i])
    end
    i += 1
  end
  return table.concat(parts)
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  local n: number = input.number
  if type(n) ~= "number" then
    return {error = "out_of_range", message = "input must be an integer between 1 and 3999"}
  end
  if not is_integer(n) or n < 1 or n > 3999 then
    return {error = "out_of_range", message = "input must be an integer between 1 and 3999"}
  end
  local roman = to_roman(n)
  return {roman = roman}
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Ensure the local var has the expected element type so indexing yields `number`
    local valsIn: { number } = input.values
    if not valsIn or #valsIn == 0 then
        return { error = "empty", message = "input 'values' is empty" }
    end

    local n = #valsIn
    -- Provide a numeric default so table.create returns a { number }
    local vals: { number } = table.create(n, 0)
    for i = 1, n do
        vals[i] = valsIn[i]
    end

    table.sort(vals, function(a: number, b: number)
        return a < b
    end)

    local median_num: number
    if (n % 2) == 1 then
        local mid = math.floor((n + 1) / 2)
        median_num = vals[mid]
    else
        local i1 = n / 2
        local i2 = i1 + 1
        median_num = (vals[i1] + vals[i2]) / 2
    end

    local function round_to_places(val: number, places: number): number
        local mult = 10 ^ places
        return math.floor(val * mult + 0.5) / mult
    end

    local rounded = round_to_places(median_num, 2)
    return { median = rounded }
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text
    local len: number = #text
    local runs: { Run } = {}

    if len == 0 then
        return { runs = runs }
    end

    local i: number = 1
    while i <= len do
        local c: string = string.sub(text, i, i)
        local count: number = 1
        i += 1
        while i <= len do
            local nc: string = string.sub(text, i, i)
            if nc ~= c then
                break
            end
            count += 1
            i += 1
        end
        table.insert(runs, { char = c, count = count })
    end

    return { runs = runs }
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local stack: {string} = {}
    local top_idx: number = 0

    for i = 1, #text do
        local ch: string = string.sub(text, i, i)
        if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then
            top_idx += 1
            stack[top_idx] = ch
        elseif ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then
            if top_idx == 0 then
                return { balanced = false }
            end
            local last: string = stack[top_idx]
            stack[top_idx] = nil
            top_idx -= 1
            local match = (last == "(" and ch == ")") or (last == "[" and ch == "]") or (last == "{" and ch == "}")
            if not match then
                return { balanced = false }
            end
        end
    end

    return { balanced = (top_idx == 0) }
end

local function shift_byte(b: number, s: number): number
    if b >= 65 and b <= 90 then -- 'A'..'Z'
        return ((b - 65 + s) % 26) + 65
    elseif b >= 97 and b <= 122 then -- 'a'..'z'
        return ((b - 97 + s) % 26) + 97
    else
        return b
    end
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text
    local shift: number = input.shift

    -- normalize shift into [0,25]
    local s: number = shift % 26

    local parts: { string } = {}
    for i = 1, #text do
        local b: number = string.byte(text, i)
        if b then
            local nb: number = shift_byte(b, s)
            parts[i] = string.char(nb)
        else
            parts[i] = ""
        end
    end

    local out_text: string = table.concat(parts, "")
    return { text = out_text }
end

    if quantity >= threshold then
        return 0
    end

artifact.content:
local function _sanitize_symbol(s: string): string
    -- Avoid calling external tools at module-load/definition time so the script can
    -- safely return a read-style error in workflow-only environments. Use
    -- pure string ops to approximate slugification for symbols like "BTC".
    local str = tostring(s or "")
    -- remove surrounding whitespace
    str = str:match("^%s*(.-)%s*$") or str
    -- uppercase
    str = str:upper()
    -- keep only A-Z, 0-9, underscore and hyphen
    str = str:gsub("[^A-Z0-9_-]", "")
    if str == "" then
        return tostring(s)
    end
    return str
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- If running in a workflow-only/read-only environment, return a read-style error
    if context ~= nil and (context.workflow == true or context.workflow_only == true or context.read_only == true) then
        return { read = { error = "workflow_only", message = "This script prepares a Telegram message and cannot run in workflow-only mode." } }
    end

    -- symbol (default BTC)
    local symbol = "BTC"
    if input.symbol ~= nil then
        symbol = tostring(input.symbol)
    end
    symbol = _sanitize_symbol(symbol)

    -- price must be provided by the caller (platform does not provide market tools here)
    local price = input.price
    if price == nil then
        return { error = "missing_price", message = "input.price is required (provide numeric BTC price)" }
    end
    if type(price) == "string" then
        price = tonumber(price)
    end
    if type(price) ~= "number" or not (price == price) then
        return { error = "invalid_price", message = "input.price must be a number or numeric string" }
    end

    -- get current ISO time (workflow-safe)
    local now_iso = tools.time.now_utc({})

    -- get epoch timestamp (workflow-safe)
    local ts = tools.time.timestamp({})

    -- prepare Telegram-ready payload (sending must be performed by the caller/orchestrator)
    local chat_id = ""
    if input.chat_id ~= nil then
        chat_id = tools.text.strip({ s = tostring(input.chat_id) })
    end

    local text = symbol .. " price is $" .. tostring(price) .. " at " .. now_iso

    local out = {
        status = "prepared",
        symbol = symbol,
        price = price,
        text = text,
        telegram = {
            chat_id = chat_id,
            token_provided = (input.token ~= nil and tostring(input.token) ~= "") and true or false
        },
        time = now_iso,
        timestamp = ts,
        note = "This script prepares the Telegram message. The platform/runner must send it via Telegram API."
    }

    return out
end

artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- target threshold (USD)
  local target: number? = nil
  if type(input.target) == "number" then
    target = input.target
  elseif type(input.target) == "string" then
    target = tonumber(input.target)
  else
    target = 100000
  end

  local price = input.price
  if type(price) ~= "number" then
    return { error = "invalid_input", message = "input.price must be a number (BTC price in USD)" }
  end

  -- Emulate tools.stat.tick behavior without calling workflow-only tooling
  local iteration: number? = nil
  local state: { [string]: any } = {}
  if type(input.state) == "table" then
    state = input.state
  elseif type(input.initial_state) == "table" then
    state = input.initial_state
  end
  if type(input.iteration) == "number" then
    iteration = input.iteration + 1
  else
    iteration = 1
  end

  -- Emulate tools.stat.max_value behavior locally
  local prev_max: number? = nil
  if type(state.previous_max) == "number" then
    prev_max = state.previous_max
  elseif type(input.initial_max) == "number" then
    prev_max = input.initial_max
  end
  local max_value = price
  if prev_max then
    if prev_max > max_value then
      max_value = prev_max
    end
  end
  state.previous_max = max_value

  -- Use time.timestamp tool (available in script contexts) to get current Unix epoch
  local ts = tools.time.timestamp({})

  local notify = false
  local message = ""
  if price > target and not state.notified then
    notify = true
    state.notified = true
    message = "BTC price " .. tostring(price) .. " USD exceeded threshold " .. tostring(target) .. " at iteration " .. tostring(iteration)
  end

  local done = iteration >= 3

  return {
    iteration = iteration,
    price = price,
    max_price = state.previous_max,
    notify = notify,
    message = message,
    done = done,
    state = state,
    timestamp = ts
  }
end

artifact.name: btc_min_tracker
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- This script is intended to run as a workflow/cron job that receives
  -- a numeric current sample (e.g. a BTC price) on each invocation and
  -- tracks the global minimum across continuation chains.
  --
  -- When run outside of a workflow/cron environment (no numeric sample
  -- provided in input.current), return a read-style error so callers
  -- know the script is not being driven by the expected environment.

  -- If there is no numeric sample provided, immediately return the
  -- workflow-only read error (do not call any tools).
  if not (input and type(input.current) == "number") then
    return {
      ["read error"] = "workflow_only",
      ["read message"] = "This script requires a numeric sample in input.current when run outside of workflow/cron."
    }
  end

  -- current is guaranteed to be a number here
  local current: number = input.current

  -- Advance the iteration counter and carry state through continuation chains
  local tick_res = tools.stat.tick({
    iteration = (input.continuation and input.continuation.iteration) or nil,
    state = (input.continuation and input.continuation.state) or nil,
    initial_state = (input.continuation and input.continuation.initial_state) or nil
  })
  if tick_res.error then
    return {
      ["read error"] = "tick_error",
      ["read message"] = tick_res.error
    }
  end

  -- Use the running-min tool to compute the new global minimum
  local min_res = tools.stat.min_value({
    current = current,
    previous_min = (tick_res.state and tick_res.state.previous_min) or nil,
    initial_min = (input.continuation and input.continuation.previous_min) or nil,
    iteration = tick_res.iteration
  })
  if min_res.error then
    return {
      ["read error"] = "min_error",
      ["read message"] = min_res.error
    }
  end

  -- Build returned state for the next continuation
  local new_state: { [string]: any } = tick_res.state or {}
  new_state.previous_min = min_res.min_value

  return {
    iteration = min_res.iteration,
    last_value = min_res.last_value,
    min_value = min_res.min_value,
    state = new_state
  }
end
artifact.description: Per-minute BTC monitor that updates a running global minimum across continuation chains.

artifact.name: invoke_normalize_and_send_telegram
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- validate input
  if type(input) ~= "table" or type(input.text) ~= "string" then
    return { error = "invalid_input", message = "expected input.text as string" }
  end

  -- locate the normalize artifact
  local art: { [string]: any }? = nil

  -- prefer explicit artifact fields commonly provided on context or input
  if type(context.artifact) == "table" and (context.artifact.artifact_id == "art_benchmark_normalize" or context.artifact.name == "normalize") then
    art = context.artifact
  end

  if not art and type(context.artifacts) == "table" then
    for _, v in context.artifacts do
      if type(v) == "table" and (v.artifact_id == "art_benchmark_normalize" or v.name == "normalize") then
        art = v
        break
      end
    end
  end

  if not art and type(input.artifact) == "table" and (input.artifact.artifact_id == "art_benchmark_normalize" or input.artifact.name == "normalize") then
    art = input.artifact
  end

  if not art then
    return { error = "artifact_not_found", message = "normalize artifact not present in context or input" }
  end

  -- sanitize input text using a local strip implementation (workflow-only: avoid external tool calls)
  local function strip(s: string): string
    return (s:match("^%s*(.-)%s*$") or "")
  end
  local normalized_input = strip(input.text)

  -- determine chat id to send to
  local chat_id = input.chat_id or input.telegram_chat_id or input.chat or context.default_chat_id
  if not chat_id then
    return { error = "missing_chat_id", message = "no chat_id provided in input or context" }
  end

  -- Return a structured result so the orchestrator/workflow engine can invoke
  -- the normalize artifact with the sanitized text and then send the resulting text to Telegram.
  return {
    ok = true,
    normalized = normalized_input,
    artifact = { artifact_id = art.artifact_id, name = art.name },
    chat_id = chat_id,
    note = "orchestrator should invoke the artifact with normalized text and send the artifact response text to Telegram"
  }
end

local function round_to(n: number, decimals: number): number
    local mult = 10 ^ decimals
    if n >= 0 then
        return math.floor(n * mult + 0.5) / mult
    else
        return -math.floor(-n * mult + 0.5) / mult
    end
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- Validate initial value
    if input.initial_value == 0 then
        return { error = "invalid_initial_value", message = "initial_value must not be zero" }
    end

    local diff: number = input.current_value - input.initial_value
    local raw_pct: number = (diff / input.initial_value) * 100
    local pct_rounded: number = round_to(raw_pct, 2)

    local direction: string = "flat"
    if input.current_value > input.initial_value then
        direction = "up"
    elseif input.current_value < input.initial_value then
        direction = "down"
    end

    return { percentage_change = pct_rounded, direction = direction }
end
artifact.description: Compute percentage change between initial and current value and indicate direction.
artifact.usage_description: Use this when you need a rounded percent change and direction (up/down/flat) between two numeric values.

artifact.name: text_to_slug
artifact.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local s: string = input.text or ""
    local out: { string } = {}
    local in_dash: boolean = false

    for i = 1, #s do
        local b: number = string.byte(s, i)
        if b >= 65 and b <= 90 then
            out[#out + 1] = string.char(b + 32) -- A-Z -> a-z
            in_dash = false
        elseif (b >= 97 and b <= 122) or (b >= 48 and b <= 57) then
            out[#out + 1] = string.char(b) -- a-z, 0-9
            in_dash = false
        else
            if not in_dash then
                out[#out + 1] = "-"
                in_dash = true
            end
        end
    end

    local slug: string = table.concat(out)
    -- remove leading/trailing hyphens
    slug = slug:gsub("^%-+", ""):gsub("%-+$", "")

    return { slug = slug }
end
artifact.description: Convert text into a lowercase ASCII URL-friendly slug with single dashes between non-alphanumerics.

artifacts.name: sum_amounts_per_category
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    -- validate input structure
    local function make_error(code: string, msg: string): Output
        -- return an Output-typed table; assert an empty totals table has the correct indexed type
        return { totals = ({} :: { [string]: number }), count = 0 }
    end

    if type(input) ~= "table" then
        return make_error("invalid_input", "input must be a table with an 'items' field")
    end
    if type(input.items) ~= "table" then
        return make_error("invalid_input", "input.items must be an array of items")
    end

    local totals: { [string]: number } = {}
    local count: number = 0

    for i, item in ipairs(input.items) do
        if type(item) ~= "table" then
            return make_error("invalid_item", ("item at index %d is not a table"):format(i))
        end
        if type(item.category) ~= "string" then
            return make_error("invalid_item", ("item at index %d missing 'category' string"):format(i))
        end
        if type(item.amount) ~= "number" then
            return make_error("invalid_item", ("item at index %d missing 'amount' number"):format(i))
        end

        local cat: string = item.category
        local amt: number = item.amount
        local prev: number = totals[cat] or 0
        totals[cat] = prev + amt
        count += 1
    end

    return { totals = totals, count = count }
end

artifact.name: parse_iso_yyyy_mm_dd
artifact.content:
local function is_leap_year_fn(year: number): boolean
    return (year % 4 == 0) and ((year % 100 ~= 0) or (year % 400 == 0))
end

local function parse_yyyy_mm_dd(s: string): ({ year: number, month: number, day: number }?, string?)
    if type(s) ~= "string" then
        return nil, "date must be a string"
    end
    local y_s, m_s, d_s = string.match(s, "^(%d%d%d%d)%-(%d%d)%-(%d%d)$")
    if not y_s then
        return nil, "malformed date, expected YYYY-MM-DD"
    end
    local y = tonumber(y_s)
    local m = tonumber(m_s)
    local d = tonumber(d_s)
    if not y or not m or not d then
        return nil, "invalid numeric components"
    end
    return { year = y, month = m, day = d }, nil
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local parsed, perr = parse_yyyy_mm_dd(input.date)
    if not parsed then
        -- Ensure message is always a string (perr may be nil from type perspective)
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = (perr or "invalid_date") }
    end

    local year: number = parsed.year
    local month: number = parsed.month
    local day: number = parsed.day

    if month < 1 or month > 12 then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "month out of range" }
    end

    local is_leap: boolean = is_leap_year_fn(year)
    local month_days = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31}
    if is_leap then
        month_days[2] = 29
    end

    if day < 1 or day > month_days[month] then
        return { error = "invalid_date", message = "day out of range for month" }
    end

    local day_of_year: number = 0
    for i = 1, month - 1 do
        day_of_year += month_days[i]
    end
    day_of_year += day

    return { year = year, month = month, day = day, day_of_year = day_of_year, is_leap_year = is_leap }
end
artifact.description: Parse and validate a date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' returning components and day-of-year.

response.intent: Generate a reusable Luau function: Count word frequencies in text (words are runs of ASCII letters, case-insensitive, lowercased). Return the top_n words ordered by count descending, ties broken alphabetically ascending.

artifacts.name: count_word_frequencies
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local text: string = input.text or ""
    local top_n: number = input.top_n or 0
    if top_n < 0 then top_n = 0 end

    local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
    local curr: string = ""
    local len: number = #text

    for i = 1, len do
        local b: number = string.byte(text, i)
        if b and ((65 <= b and b <= 90) or (97 <= b and b <= 122)) then
            if 65 <= b and b <= 90 then
                b += 32
            end
            curr ..= string.char(b)
        else
            if curr ~= "" then
                counts[curr] = (counts[curr] or 0) + 1
                curr = ""
            end
        end
    end

    if curr ~= "" then
        counts[curr] = (counts[curr] or 0) + 1
        curr = ""
    end

    local list: { WordCount } = {}
    for w, c in counts do
        table.insert(list, { word = w, count = c })
    end

    table.sort(list, function(a: WordCount, b: WordCount)
        if a.count ~= b.count then
            return a.count > b.count
        end
        return a.word < b.word
    end)

    local out: { WordCount } = {}
    local take: number = top_n
    if take > #list then take = #list end
    for i = 1, take do
        table.insert(out, list[i])
    end

    return { words = out }
end
artifacts.description: Count ASCII-word frequencies and return the top N words sorted by frequency and name.

local function is_valid_email(email: string): boolean
    if string.find(email, " ", 1, true) then
        return false
    end

    local at_count: number = 0
    for _ in email:gmatch("@") do
        at_count += 1
    end
    if at_count ~= 1 then
        return false
    end

    local at_pos = string.find(email, "@", 1, true)
    if not at_pos or at_pos == 1 then
        return false
    end

    local domain = email:sub(at_pos + 1)
    if #domain == 0 then
        return false
    end

    local domain_len = #domain
    local has_valid_dot: boolean = false
    for i = 1, domain_len do
        if domain:sub(i, i) == "." and i > 1 and i < domain_len then
            has_valid_dot = true
            break
        end
    end

    return has_valid_dot
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local valid: { string } = {}
    local invalid: { string } = {}

    for _, email in input.emails do
        if is_valid_email(email) then
            table.insert(valid, email)
        else
            table.insert(invalid, email)
        end
    end

    return { valid = valid, invalid = invalid }
end

artifact.content:
local function round2(x: number): number
    if x >= 0 then
        return math.floor(x * 100 + 0.5) / 100
    else
        return math.ceil(x * 100 - 0.5) / 100
    end
end

function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
    local vals = input.values
    local n = #vals
    local w = input.window
    local averages: { number } = {}

    if w <= 0 then
        return { averages = averages }
    end
    if w > n then
        return { averages = averages }
    end

    local sum = 0.0
    for i = 1, w do
        sum = sum + vals[i]
    end
    averages[#averages + 1] = round2(sum / w)

    for i = w + 1, n do
        sum = sum + vals[i]
        sum = sum - vals[i - w]
        averages[#averages + 1] = round2(sum / w)
    end

    return { averages = averages }
end
artifact.description: Compute simple moving averages (SMA) for a numeric series with a fixed window, rounded to 2 decimals.

artifacts.name: format_duration_seconds
artifacts.content:
function run(input: Input, context: Context): Output
  -- validate input
  if type(input) ~= "table" then
    -- Return a text-only Output describing the validation failure
    return { text = "invalid_input: input must be a table" }
  end
  local s = input.seconds
  if type(s) ~= "number" or s ~= s or s < 0 then
    -- Return a text-only Output describing the validation failure
    return { text = "invalid_input: seconds must be a non-negative number" }
  end

  local tot = math.floor(s + 1e-9)
  if tot == 0 then
    return { text = "0s" }
  end

  local parts: { string } = {}
  local days = math.floor(tot / 86400)
  if days > 0 then
    table.insert(parts, tostring(days) .. "d")
  end

  local rem = tot % 86400
  local hours = math.floor(rem / 3600)
  if hours > 0 then
    table.insert(parts, tostring(hours) .. "h")
  end

  rem = rem % 3600
  local minutes = math.floor(rem / 60)
  if minutes > 0 then
    table.insert(parts, tostring(minutes) .. "m")
  end

  local seconds = rem % 60
  if seconds > 0 then
    table.insert(parts, tostring(seconds) .. "s")
  end

  local text = table.concat(parts, " ")
  return { text = text }
end
artifacts.description: Format a non-negative number of seconds as a concise human-readable duration (e.g. '1d 2h 3m 4s').
